questions.stem: Which document is issued by the seller to request payment for goods sold?
questions.explanation: An invoice is the document that requests payment for goods sold, detailing the items and total amount due.

distractorRationale.a: The delivery note simply lists the items delivered and does not request payment.
distractorRationale.b: A credit note acknowledges a return or adjustment and does not request payment.
distractorRationale.c: A debit note indicates a return of goods but is not used to request payment.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a delivery note?
questions.explanation: A delivery note lists the items that have been delivered to the buyer, ensuring that they receive what they ordered.

distractorRationale.a: A delivery note does not confirm payment; that is the role of a receipt.
distractorRationale.b: It does not request a quotation; that is the purpose of an enquiry.
distractorRationale.c: A delivery note does not issue a credit; that is done through a credit note.

questions.stem: Which document would you use to acknowledge a return of goods?
questions.explanation: A credit note is issued to acknowledge the return of goods and adjust the buyer's account accordingly.

distractorRationale.a: An invoice requests payment, not acknowledges returns.
distractorRationale.b: A delivery note lists items delivered, not returned.
distractorRationale.c: A quotation provides pricing information, not return acknowledgments.
